#2822. Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings suspended one game for elbow to the head

The NBA has suspended Atlanta Hawks point guard Kingston Flemings, the league announced on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Flemings will sit out one game without pay after the league ruled that he intentionally elbowed New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head during their matchup on Saturday, Oct. 31.

The rookie made contact with McGowens in back-to-back plays in the Hawks' 121-99 loss at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans. With just over three minutes left in the fourth quarter, Flemings drove for a layup and his elbow hit McGowens in the face as the defender blocked the shot.

Trey Murphy III grabbed the rebound from Flemings' miss and tossed the ball to Zion Williamson. The two-time All-Star tossed it back to Murphy, who slammed home a dunk to make the score 119-93. In the background, Flemings threw an elbow at McGowens' head as they were following the play downcourt. The two teams scuffled at center court.

Upon review, Flemings was given a technical foul and ejected from the game. The Pelicans' Julian Reese was also handed a technical foul "for not being a peacemaker during the melee."

Flemings, who is averaging 7.1 points per matchup in seven games off the bench, spoke to reporters after the loss and explained how frustration got the best of him.

"Upset we were losing the game, so definitely apologize for that," he said. "Gotta be smarter than that."

He will sit out the Hawks' road game against the Indiana Pacers on Monday, Nov. 2.

#2819. Jack Campbell Injury: Everything We Know After Frightening Scene at Ford Field

The Detroit Lions picked up one of their biggest victories of the season Sunday, defeating the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings 19-15 at Ford Field. But the celebration was understandably subdued following a frightening injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell.

Campbell was taken off the field on a backboard and transported to a local hospital, leaving teammates visibly shaken and Lions fans across the country searching for updates.

Since then, Detroit has released an official statement, while head coach Dan Campbell has provided additional information about his linebacker.

Here is everything we currently know about Jack Campbell's injury as of Monday morning, November 2, 2026.

Detroit Lions medical staff check on linebacker Jack Campbell's injury during the second half between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The incident occurred with 14:48 remaining in the fourth quarter, as Campbell was involved in a tackle of former Lions tight end T.J. Hockenson.

Campbell remained face down on the turf following the play, prompting medical personnel to rush onto the field. The game was stopped for approximately nine to ten minutes while he received attention.

Medical personnel eventually secured Campbell to a backboard before carefully lifting him onto a cart. He was subsequently transported to a local hospital for further evaluation.

As we reported Sunday following the frightening scene at Ford Field, Detroit's defensive players gathered in prayer while Campbell received medical attention.

Aidan Hutchinson was visibly emotional, and players and coaches surrounded the cart before their teammate was taken away.

Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was also injured on the play, leaving the game with a hamstring injury.

One of the most important updates came directly from Lions head coach Dan Campbell following the game.

Speaking with Brad Galli during a postgame interview on the Lions Radio Network, Campbell provided an encouraging piece of information about Jack's condition when he departed the stadium.

"He's breathing, he's alert when he left. I know nothing further. Thoughts and prayers are with Jack. I would ask that everyone does the same," Dan Campbell said.

That was significant information following an extremely concerning scene on the field.

However, being alert does not establish the nature or severity of an injury. The Lions have not released specific medical findings or publicly confirmed Campbell's neurological status.

Several hours after Sunday's game, the Lions issued a formal announcement regarding Campbell's condition.

"Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them," the organization announced.

As we reported Sunday evening when that statement was released, Campbell was expected to spend the night at the hospital rather than return home immediately.

The statement established that Campbell was resting and continuing to undergo medical evaluation. It did not disclose a diagnosis, the results of any tests, or whether additional treatment would be necessary.

As of Monday morning, there has been no verified announcement confirming that Campbell has been released from the hospital.

This remains the biggest unanswered question.

Although Campbell was immobilized before leaving the field, the Lions have not publicly announced a definitive medical diagnosis or established the severity of his injury.

The team has also not confirmed whether Campbell has full movement and sensation in his extremities.

That lack of information should not be interpreted as evidence of any particular medical condition. It simply means those details have not been publicly established.

Any specific diagnosis or prediction about Campbell's recovery would be speculation at this point.

Campbell's injury clearly affected his teammates, several of whom spoke about the incident following Detroit's victory.

Quarterback Jared Goff emphasized that Campbell's well-being mattered far more than anything happening on the football field.

"Jack's deal was definitely scary," Goff said following the victory. "It just brings you back to reality for a moment that he's a husband and a father. Scary. We're praying for him and hope he's going to be alright. If anyone is tough enough to get through something like that it's going to be him."

Dan Campbell also led the team in prayer during his postgame locker-room address, underscoring the concern surrounding one of Detroit's defensive leaders.

The 26-year-old linebacker has become a central figure in the Lions' defense since arriving as a first-round draft pick in 2023. He earned first-team All-Pro honors last season and signed a contract extension through 2030.

There is currently no confirmed timetable for Campbell's return.

Detroit has not announced whether he will be available for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, nor has the organization provided an estimate for how much time he could miss.

The next significant development will be an official medical update or an announcement concerning his hospital status.

For now, the most important confirmed information is that Campbell was breathing and alert when he left Ford Field, was resting at a local hospital Sunday evening, and remained under medical evaluation and monitoring overnight.

His diagnosis, recovery outlook, and potential return to football are still unknown.

The Lions have promised to share additional information when it becomes available. Until then, everyone associated with the organization is hoping for the best possible news regarding one of its most respected players.

#2813. Can Fantasy Football Managers Trust Jonah Coleman In Week 9 And Moving Forward With Jonathan Taylor Looming?

We had another exciting fantasy football Sunday in Week 8, and it was especially exciting for Jonah Coleman owners. The rookie had his breakout game, but we've seen running backs do this in Denver in the past, then fizzle out. That leads us to one obvious question: can you trust Denver Broncos rookie running back moving forward?

In Week 8, Coleman dominated the Broncos' backfield, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps, with JK Dobbins playing on just 21%. Coleman carried the ball 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown, and caught four of his five targets for another 63 yards. Dobbins took just seven carries for 13 yards and wasn't targeted in the passing attack.

It does not seem like a fading Dobbins is going to be a significant issue. That doesn't mean he won't play more than he did this week, but we are confident that Coleman will be the lead back.

However, RJ Harvey could return after three more games. If Dobbins continues to see around seven carries, and Harvey cuts into Coleman's passing-down work, it could cap his upside. Nevertheless, that won't be anytime in the immediate future, with Harvey being placed on injured reserve last week.

There is also another looming threat that could be a major issue for Coleman. The Broncos are one of the teams that have been linked to a potential trade for Jonathan Taylor.

The hope is that Coleman played well enough to convince the Broncos they don't need Taylor. Nevertheless, if they do end up trading for JT, he is going to be the bell-cow back in Denver. Still, there have been a handful of teams linked to Taylor, and this is far from a lock.

There are some potential pitfalls, but we are going to roll with the rookie. We projected him to take over the starting job in Denver around midseason, and that's exactly what's happening. It would be crazy to back off of what we've said along as we see it happening in real time.

As long as they don't make a move for Taylor, which we aren't expecting, you can trust Coleman moving forward. We don't view either Dobbins or Harvey as serious threats. Although they could cut into his workload a bit at times, it will not be enough to seriously damage his fantasy viability.

#2809. Dan Campbell wisely declined the Vikings' intentional offsides

With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday in Detroit, the Lions had a 19-15 lead and the ball, facing second-and-2. Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel jumped offside, and fans in Detroit cheered, thinking the Vikings had made a mistake. But Lions coach Dan Campbell knew better.

Campbell declined the penalty because he knew the Vikings had jumped offside on purpose, wanting to concede a first down while the clock was stopped so that they could then use their three timeouts after the Lions’ first, second and third-down plays and then get the ball back with time left for a comeback drive.

Tom Brady, calling the game on Fox, immediately recognized what was happening.

“They’re not gonna accept that,” Brady said as soon as Van Ginkel jumped. “They’ll decline that penalty.”

It was obvious to Brady, but it wasn’t obvious to Bears coach Ben Johnson when he faced the same situation against the Patriots. Coach Mike Vrabel told his team to jump offside to concede a first down, and Johnson accepted the penalty. That allowed the Patriots to use their three timeouts on the Bears’ next three plays, forcing the Bears to kick on fourth down with 1:38 remaining. The Bears ended up winning when kicker Cairo Santos made it a two-possession game with a 58-yard field goal, but if the Bears had missed, Johnson’s decision to accept the penalty could have proven costly.

It’s a situation that doesn’t arise in most games, but it happens often enough that every coach should understand it as well as Vrabel, Campbell and Brady do: Sometimes, the smart thing for one team is to commit a penalty on purpose, and the smart thing for the other team is to decline the penalty.

In theory, if the defensive team continued to jump offside and the offense continued to decline the penalties, it could reach the point where the referee would have to warn the defensive team’s head coach that he could invoke the “palpably unfair act” rule, which gives the referee wide leeway to use his own discretion to enforce penalties. The referee could, for instance, charge the defensive team a timeout if it refused to stop committing intentional penalties.

It didn’t reach that point on Sunday, as Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell realized that Campbell was on to the intentional offside. Campbell is a smart in-game coach who recognized on Sunday what the right strategic decision was in the final two minutes.

#2805. Saquon Barkley: Eagles said they won't trade me, I want to be here to fix it

A report before Sunday’s games said that the Eagles will not trade running back Saquon Barkley ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and Barkley said after Sunday night’s game against the Commanders that he’s received the same message from the team.

Barkley played through hamstring and back injuries in that game and he scored a touchdown in the first quarter, but the Eagles went from being up 10-0 to losing 27-10 in Washington. The loss was the sixth in a row for a team that’s reeling, but Barkley made it clear that he’s not looking to jump ship and is happy that the Eagles aren’t interested in parting ways.

“When that message was relayed to me, it definitely does mean a lot,” Barkley said, via Tim McManus of ESPN.com. “The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I’m the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it, and I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it.”

The Eagles traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens last month and their tailspin would seem to make more deals a real possibility, but Barkley is set to be around for the long haul.

#2801. Lakers' Luka Doncic makes history twice, fills up stat sheet vs Raptors

The Los Angeles Lakers put away the Toronto Raptors, thanks in no small part to another monster game from Luka Dončić, who scored 45 points and filled up the stat sheet as he continues to make an early-season case for MVP honors.

Coming off a disappointing loss to the Golden State Warriors on Friday, Oct. 30, in which they faded after a fast start, the Lakers returned to Crypto.com Arena Sunday, Nov. 1 and got off to a fast start, with Dončić being particularly active on both ends of the floor. The Slovenian superstar finished the first half with 24 points, eight rebounds, four assists and a career-high five steals – four of which came in the first quarter.

"Luka doesn't get enough credit for his defense," Lakers center Walker Kessler said. "He's a very high IQ individual when it comes to being on the court, so his positional defense, just being in the right spots at the right time, is really good and it showed tonight."

Then there's also a bit of history he made: Dončić became the first NBA player in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98) with 20 points, five rebounds, five three-pointers and five steals in a half and the first point guard in NBA history with five steals and five three-pointers in a half.

The guard also became the first player in the league's history to record at least 45 points, 15 rebounds, 5 assists, 5 steals and 5 3-pointers made in a game.

The six-time All-Star and two-time scoring champ finished the game with eight 3-pointers, one shy of his career high.

Dončić was on quadruple-double watch early, especially with his five first-half steals, but he was not able to add to that category. Still, he finished with his second double-double of the season and his fourth in a row scoring at least 35 points even as the Raptors clawed their way back from a big deficit by outscoring the Lakers 43-27 in the fourth quarter.

It remains unclear if Dončić will play in the second game of a back-to-back on Monday against the Miami Heat.

"I got to get rest, a cold tub, a massage, and rest and see you tomorrow," Dončić told Spectrum SportsNet after the game on Sunday night.

#2797. Premier League legend James Milner runs NYC Marathon in 3:09

James Milner is not slowing down in retirement.

The Premier League's record appearance-maker retired at the end of the 2025-26 season, but he is still taking on new athletic challenges.

Milner took part in his first marathon on Sunday, Nov. 1, but the 40-year-old didn't look like a novice runner.

Milner completed the 2026 New York City Marathon with a time of 3:09:04, an average of 7:13 per mile.

He represented Leeds, Newcastle, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton through a 24-year career, ending with a record 658 Premier League appearances.

Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes celebrates scoring against Ipswich on Aug. 30, 2026. Manchester United won the match, 5-2.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez celebrates his team scoring against Brighton on Aug. 30, 2026. Chelsea won the match, 4-3.

Sunderland fans celebrate a goal against Fulham on Aug. 30, 2026. Sunderland won the match, 1-0.

Sunderland's Granit Xhaka celebrates after a 1-0 win against Fulham on Aug. 30, 2026.

Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes celebrates scoring against Ipswich on Aug. 30, 2026. Manchester United won the match, 5-2.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez celebrates his team scoring against Brighton on Aug. 30, 2026. Chelsea won the match, 4-3.

Sunderland fans celebrate a goal against Fulham on Aug. 30, 2026. Sunderland won the match, 1-0.

Sunderland's Granit Xhaka celebrates after a 1-0 win against Fulham on Aug. 30, 2026.

Milner was known for his fitness during his playing career, but retirement has allowed him to fully pursue his new goal of distance running.

"I've always had a pretty good engine," he told LetsRun.com before the marathon.

"But then the last few years, when you get a bit older, you have to look after yourself a bit more in football. So I was stopped from running in pre-season and things like that."

Despite significant injury issues late in his career, Milner still came within 10 minutes of the sub-three-hour marathon he once believed he could run.

"A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00," he said. "My career went on longer and longer. Two years ago, I had a knee operation, and when I woke up from the knee operation, I couldn't lift my foot. And I had a second operation that day to check, and then I couldn't lift my foot for six months. I had nerve damage.

"So I feel to go from not being able to walk properly and maybe never being able to walk to coming back, playing football in the Premier League, and hopefully potentially finishing a marathon, I don't want to get too much caught up on the time."

#2796. Joe Burrow: We found a way to win, we didn't do that the last few years

The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they’re ready to start playing football this season.

The Bengals spotted the Ravens that lead in the first half of Week 7 before rallying for a 35-13 win and they found themselves down 13-0 in the first quarter against the Titans this Sunday. They didn’t wait until the second half to get their act together this week, but they had to struggle the whole way before finally nailing down a 43-36 overtime win.

Burrow and others fielded questions about their slow starts in their postgame press conferences, but Burrow was more interested in the final scores because he feels that scrapping out wins like their last two are a sign that the team has fixed part of what has ailed them the last few years.

“We found a way to win today. We’re 5-2,” Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. “We lose that game for the last three years. It’s hard to win. You want to be great snap in snap out, but it’s not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That’s what the NFL and getting better is. We’ll continue to do that.”

Burrow threw three interceptions to go with five touchdown passes and his game-winning touchdown run on Sunday. He acknowledged the need to “be better and limit those critical mistakes,” but returned often to the theme of finding ways to win when they would have fallen apart in the past.

This meant that Union were unbeaten in three games in a row before being thrashed by Köln on Tuesday.

In spite of this, one thing that does not bode well for the capital city side is their form in front of goal.

Union have the joint-second least amount of goals in the league this season only having scored more than Schalke.

Köln are looking to pick up their first three points away from home in over a year on the road in the Bundesliga in a season where their home and away form has been completely opposite.

Alongside RB Leipzig, Köln are the only side yet to pick up even a point away from home this Bundesliga season with losses against Frankfurt, Stuttgart and Hamburg.

In midweek, youngster Said El Mala had his best game for Köln ever with two goals and an assist picking up man of the match in the cup.

Before the weekend game against Union Berlin, head coach Rene Wagner said: “It's a different game from Tuesday. Union will be fired up and looking to show some sort of reaction. They have been playing well at home. ”

Köln are without Imad Rondić, Thijs Dallinga, Ellyes Skhiri, Timo Hübers and Rav Van den Berg.

#2792. USC football's biggest studs and duds from Week 9 vs Ohio State

It is no longer a secret who the USC Trojans' offense should run through. It's also no secret who the best players on that unit actually are. This was a complete game across the board for the Trojans, as both the defense and offense stepped up big time against Ohio State. That was due to the best players on the team having their best games.

Here are the biggest studs and duds from the USC Trojans' seventh game of the season:

The run game as a whole was a huge reason for the Trojans' success offensively. On just 13 carries, King Miller ran for 78 yards and a touchdown. He had a 6.0 yards-per-carry average, and his physicality set the tone. He picked up 4 first downs on the ground. It was not just his impact with the ball in his hands; he also made a touchdown-sealing block for his running mate, Waymond Jordan, to find the end zone.

Waymond Jordan did not play the previous week against the Wisconsin Badgers. He came into this game and delivered in his snaps. Jordan had 12 carries for 48 yards, but his touchdown put an exclamation point on what kind of game it was going to be. Jordan will continue to have an impact moving forward, and that is great for the Trojans' offense.

Jeremiah Smith, who? Trent Mosley was the best receiver in this game. Mosley kicked off the game with a 69-yard screen pass for a touchdown. Mosley finished the game with 5 catches for 101 yards. Mosley also had a 44-yard punt return to put the icing on the cake for his dominant game.

Mark Bowman's return for the USC Trojans took their offense to the next level. Bowman had just 3 catches for 79 yards. He had the play of the game and maybe the best play in recent memory for USC. His athleticism was on full display as he hurdled a Buckeyes defender and plowed through many defenders for a 70-yard gain. When that play happened, it was clear USC was going to win this game.

Last week against the Badgers. This week it was a completely different story. Elijah Paige was dominant, and every other player on this unit showed up. The Trojans do not run the football as effectively as they did without the big 5 guys up front playing at an elite level. Their play made the biggest difference in this game.

Alex VanSumeren was a key performer upfront. He had 3 tackles and joined in with Kameryn Crawford for a sack. Games like this are what VanSumeren was brought in for, and it was encouraging to see him perform at a high level.

Deven Bryant was flying all over the football field. Bryant had 11 tackles, and he led the Trojans' defense to their best performance of the season. The Trojans will need this again for their next two games as the season continues to heat up.

Kayden Dixon-Wyatt was held in check and finished the game against the Buckeyes with zero catches. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt is just as exciting as freshmen Mark Bowman and Trent Mosley. This performance does not hinder the excitement around him, and he has stepped up big time all season long while his counterparts were hurt. I would not be surprised to see him bounce back against the Indiana Hoosiers and have an elite performance.

On the other hand, in the biggest game of the season for USC, and a game that USC was able to win, Tanook Hines was a non-factor. He has been a player who has underachieved, but this is a game where you would at least expect him to get a target. There are some other big games for the Trojans coming up, and he has a shot to make an impact there, but it has never been clearer who Jayden Maiava trusts the most and who his best weapons are.

The USC Trojans' defensive line had an impressive goal-line stand. The Trojans' defense made key stops against the run in important moments in the game. However, USC gave up more than they would have liked on the ground. That was the area where the Buckeyes were the most successful. Bo Jackson ran for 121 yards, and Isaiah West ran for 65 yards. Both backs had at least a 5.0-yard-per-carry average. That spells trouble in the future for USC against the UCLA Bruins.

Browns defensive end Jared Verse gave the Steelers some fuel ahead of Sunday’s games by sharing his thoughts about the team being dirty and vowing to “make Pittsburgh ours” in Week 8.

#2790. Luka Dončić carries Lakers to win over Raptors

Another night of brilliance from Luka Dončić led the Lakers to a bounceback win on Sunday as they knocked off the Raptors, 131-125.

Coming off a loss to the Warriors, LA rode Luka's back to another win as he put up another 40-point game. The team struggled mightily in the minutes without him, but still did enough to hang onto the win, barely.

The Lakers forced 15 turnovers, many of those coming in the first period, which they turned into 23 points. They offset that by turning the ball over 24 times themselves, leading to 30 Toronto points. It was a much-improved performance from the bench as well as they scored 37 points.

Luka set the tone to start the game, as he's one to do. However, this time, it came on the defensive end. The Lakers were particularly active on the defensive end, swiping seven steals in the quarter.

Behind that, LA jumped out to not only an early advantage, but a double-digit one at that. A 10-0 run all came at the hands of Luka, who hit a three, set up Matisse Thybulle for one and got assists on Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler finishes at the rim.

A 10-2 run shortly after included threes from Reaves and Sandro Mamukelashvili to build a 23-11 lead. Luka hit a pair of threes at the end of the period to help LA carry a 36-23 advantage into the second.

The Lakers were much better with Luka on the bench in this contest with Collin Sexton scoring eight points and Mamu connecting on another three to help keep LA ahead by 11 through the first nearly six minutes of the frame.

Toronto did eventually piece together a run that forced a timeout after a Jamal Shead corner 3-pointer made it just a 49-41 LA advantage. Shead converted on an and-one to trim the lead even further, but Jake LaRavia helped LA responded with consecutive threes to make it a double-digit lead once more.

Luka closed the half in style with a 30-foot 3-pointer just before the buzzer, giving the hosts a 66-54 lead at the break. It also gave him an absurd stat line of 24 points, eight rebounds, 5 steals, 4 assists and a block in 18 minutes.

Luka did not slow down in the second half as he hit a trio of threes in the opening five minutes as the lead ballooned to 18 points.

Despite picking up his fourth foul on a silly double foul, he stayed red hot throughout, upping his total to 35 as the Lakers' lead crossed the 20-point threshold. A Grimes 3-pointer to beat the shot clock late in the frame made it a 26-point lead, the largest of the night.

A small surge from the Raptors cut the gap to 21 points heading into the fourth. That run carried over into the final frame as Toronto was on a 15-4 run.

A Mamu 3-pointer stopped the bleeding only briefly before RJ Barrett pulled the visitors to within 14 to force a Lakers timeout. Luka checked back in just before the seven-minute mark with the Lakers down 12 after leading by 22 when he checked out.

Barrett knocked down another three to make it a nine-point lead. Luka answered with a layup, then Austin finished through contact at the rim to quell the Raptors' run. A pair of Luka freebies helped stabilize LA further.

The Lakers finally pieced together a string of defensive stops that eventually led to Toronto pulling their starters down 15 with just over four minutes remaining and with a game against the Clippers on Monday.

JJ Redick soon followed suit by pulling the starters up 15 with 2:28 left. Cam Carr, fresh off the injury report, made his NBA debut in the final minutes of the game.

The garbage time minutes somehow went disastrously as the Raptors went on a 12-2 run to make it a six-point game with 43 seconds left, forcing the starters back into the game.

Luka promptly launched an 80-foot pass downcourt the first time he touched the ball for a wide open Kessler dunk that effectively sealed the game.

Luka had another huge night, finishing with 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists and five steals. Austin Reaves had another quieter outing until some late buckets to help put the game away, tallying 21 points on 6-16 shooting. He did have just three turnovers to four assists.

Kessler had another double-double with 16 points and 15 rebounds. Collin Sexton was the leading scorer off the bench with 14 points while Mamu had 11 points on 4-7 shooting. Jake LaRavia pitched in eight points and Thybulle had six.

The Lakers will be right back in action on Monday against the Heat. Tip is set for 7 p.m. PT.

#2788. Balde abre la puerta a salir del Barça en el mercado de invierno

El futuro de Alejandro Balde en el FC Barcelona podría dar un giro durante el próximo mercado de invierno. El lateral izquierdo no atraviesa su mejor momento en el conjunto azulgrana y, ante la falta de oportunidades, empieza a contemplar la posibilidad de abandonar el club en enero. Según informa Mundo Deportivo, el futbolista estaría abierto a escuchar ofertas si su situación deportiva no cambia.

La situación del defensa de 23 años ha cambiado considerablemente durante los últimos meses. Balde esperaba recuperar protagonismo esta temporada, especialmente después de las dificultades físicas que han afectado a varios compañeros de la línea defensiva. Sin embargo, sus oportunidades han sido limitadas.

João Cancelo y Xavi Espart han ganado terreno en la competencia por el lateral izquierdo. De hecho, Balde ha participado en los encuentros frente al PSG, el Real Madrid y el Alavés, aunque siempre partiendo desde el banquillo. Su falta de continuidad empieza a generar dudas sobre su futuro en el equipo.

Uno de los momentos que habría marcado un punto de inflexión fue la rueda de prensa de Hansi Flick previa al encuentro contra el Alavés. El técnico alemán se refirió directamente a la situación del lateral y reconoció que actualmente no atraviesa su mejor momento de confianza.

Balde no tiene ahora la confianza que necesita en su juego, ni la convicción. Y los defensas son muy importantes

Unas declaraciones que contrastan con los mensajes anteriores del técnico, que había destacado su profesionalidad y su trabajo diario. El futbolista esperaba recibir una comunicación más directa sobre su papel dentro de la plantilla, pero gran parte de lo que conoce sobre su situación le ha llegado a través de las comparecencias públicas de Flick.

Alejandro Balde en el Trofeu Joan Gamper. Fuente: Álex Caparrós

El mercado inglés aparece como una de las alternativas para el futuro del defensa. El pasado verano, tanto el Manchester United como el Manchester City preguntaron por su situación. También hubo interés del Bayern de Múnich, aunque el conjunto alemán terminó incorporando a Nathaniel Brown.

El Manchester United vuelve a aparecer entre los posibles destinos del lateral, que vería con buenos ojos la posibilidad de probar suerte en la Premier League. Su representante, Jorge Mendes, también podría tener un papel importante a la hora de explorar las opciones del mercado.

Una eventual salida tampoco dependería únicamente de la voluntad del futbolista. El FC Barcelona necesita reforzar su defensa y no contempla fácilmente una cesión que no garantice una operación beneficiosa para sus intereses económicos. Por ello, si finalmente se abre la puerta a una marcha, un traspaso podría convertirse en la fórmula más viable.

Balde, que lleva en el club desde los 16 años, todavía tiene contrato y mantiene la esperanza de recuperar su sitio. Sin embargo, no quiere pasar otra temporada sin continuidad. El próximo mercado de invierno podría marcar un antes y un después en su trayectoria como azulgrana.

#2786. Value of Things: In the rearview mirror

Some of you are undoubtedly confused at the title. The Texans are coming off of a bye week, so what exactly are we looking at in the rearview mirror? Well, this is what we would lovingly call self-scouting. We are looking at the Texans season rankings in the various categories to see if we can identify key points that they will need to improve on for the rest of the season, Obviously, if you are 2-5 on the season then there are definitely some things to improve on.

However, not all 2-5 football teams are created equal. Teams like the Dolphins and Titans repeatedly (although not the last two weeks) get their doors blown off. The Chargers have been an absolute mess and I am watching two dreadful teams on Sunday night football as I type this. The Texans are minus seven points in point differential which would seem to predict a 3-4 or even 4-3 record in some instances. So, clearly it is not completely awful.

So, the numbers we look at could be the beginning of figuring out a way around this. The team is 1-4 in one score games. Maybe some better luck is coming their way in the second half. Maybe there is one key adjustment they can make on either side of the ball to turn their fortunes around. The main thing is that the record really doesn't accurately tell us what is going on with this football team.

Total Yards: Offense 2367/13, Defense 2394/22Rushing Yards: Offense 593/29, Defense 686/16Passing Yards: Offense 1774/6, Defense 1708/29Penalties: 58/508 (30th)Sacks: Offense 15 (17th). Defense 21 (2nd)Turnovers: Offense 3 (2nd), Defense 6 (26th)Points per game: Offense 23.6 (15th), Defense 24.3 (19th)

Obviously, many of these numbers cut both ways, but there are a few that stand out when we get to the good, bad, and ugly on the season. We usually do great, good, and bad in victory, but with the team 2-5 victory doesn't feel like the way to go. I should point out that they are mostly even in total yards and passing yards. They are in the positive on the plus/minus. It almost seems like they are finding creative ways to lose football games. This feels like a .500 team and that is where you would think they would end up.

We will actually get to C.J. Stroud later in the week, so we will not say too much on him in this space. However, there has been growth in the passing game in general. The team had some finds in the draft and free agency in terms of skill position players. Jaylin Noel looked a lot better before he went down with a season ending injury. Foster Moreau was a really good addition as a secondary tight end.

We should remember this when we are levying our complaints about free agent signings and draft picks gone wrong. Not everything is negative and not everything is positive. Most seasons have both in somewhat equal measure. The difference would be the sheer number of injuries the Texans have sustained on both sides of the ball and there is little that can be done about that.

A very significant part of me feels sorry for Nick Caley. For the last year and a half he has been the most convenient whipping boy for the fanbase and those of us at BRB have certainly participated in that whipping and I might be the most guilty party. This is where we point out that they have surrendered the second fewest turnovers in the NFL and are in the middle of the pack in points per game and total yards. So, whether or not you torch Caley depends largely on whether you are looking at it from 10,000 feet or five feet.

The closer you look the more cracks you see in the veneer. You begin to notice one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL. You notice an offense that looks dead at key points in games after the opposing polo has managed to scheme up something to stop the offense. Caley is just not good at adjusting on the fly. He can't draw up a third and one play to save his life. These are things you can't necessarily see when you look at just the aggregate data.

Maybe even more importantly, we notice that key changes to personnel seem to come too late or not at all. David Montgomery was clearly inferior to Woody Marks, but stayed in the starting lineup until he was hurt. Xavier Hutchinso is still getting snaps over Marvin Harrison Jr. and was getting them over Jaylin Noel for much of the season. Maybe even more glaring, Keelan Rutledge is one of the lowest rated guards in the NFL according to PFF, but a superior Wyatt Teller is waiting on the bench.

Evan Brown is one of the bottom five centers in the NFL and only a couple that could be called starters are listed below him. Part of this is on Nick Caserio for the players he gives to Caley. However, the other part is on Caley for not recognizing that certain guys needed to be replaced in the lineup. I know you don't want to kill Rutledge's confidence, but there comes a point when the best five guys need to be out there.

More than anything, this probably goes to DeMeco Ryans more than anything. This isn't a smash mouth running football team. It hasn't been that at any time during Ryans' tenure. I get that this is what he wants and that makes perfect sense, but at some point you need to go with what you are. You are a spread em' out passing football team. You might as well lean into that.

The words we just said about the offense could be echoed about the defense. The main difference is that the defense was supposed to be a top five unit in the NFL. They certainly have not been that with the exception of the Tennessee Titans game. I could certainly write off the Jacksonville game to the field conditions or the Buffalo and Cincinnati game to playing top five quarterbacks in the league. There comes a certain point when you run out of excuses.

There are three problems that we can isolate with the defense. The first is a lack of turnovers. Six turnovers through seven games is simply not good enough. That could be a function of performance, but it is probably more a factor of luck. Sometimes the bounces just don't go your way. Still, there were a couple of prominent opportunities for picks that would have turned two losses into wins. A 4-3 start certainly looks a lot better than 2-5.

The second problem is the same as above. Reed Blankenship is dead ass last in safeties according to PFF. I would say that we would be surprised, but PFF also rated him as one of the worst safeties last year. Somehow Caserio thought he was a good guy to sign anyway. Add in the fact that some other players (almost all in the secondary) have not played good football this year and you have the makings of a disappointing defense regardless of scheme.

That brings us to scheme. The Texans have played more lax and more bend but don't break defense. The obvious reason was to avoid big plays, but they still have given up a ton of big plays. They rely on the front four to get home and they do more often than most teams, but they need to have more consistent pressure. More importantly, they used to make life miserable for quarterbacks. Things have been way too easy for them this season. Ryans may not want to consider personnel changes or scheme changes, but after seven weeks the "it's early" mantra just isn't going to fly.

#2785. 'Like a supernova.' Luka Doncic's 45 points only eclipsed by his defense in Lakers' win

Lakers coach JJ Redick and defensive ace Walker Kessler applauded Luka Doncic for his standout defensive performance in the Lakers' 131-125 victory over the Toronto Raptors at Crypto.com Arena on Sunday.

Doncic had five steals. He took three charges. And he collected 15 defensive rebounds. Oh, and he also had 45 points and six assists. He was 12 for 23 from the field, eight for 12 from three-point range and made all 13 of his free-throws.

Read more: Lakers blow 25-point lead in double-digit loss to Warriors

But it was his defensive performance that drew the most attention on Doncic bobblehead giveaway night. As he sat in front of the media wearing a black baseball cap, Doncic was asked why he has this reputation of not being a very good defender.

"Why? I don't know," he responded. "Obviously, I'm not the best defender in the NBA, but I think this year I really took a step forward. Obviously, people are going to talk what they want to talk [about] me. ... But I know, and my team knows, that I think I'm better this year. And that helps the whole team, I think."

So would he rather win the NBA's most valuable player award, defensive player of the year award or both?

"Both," he said, laughing. "You guys vote for that."

Perhaps, it was suggested to Doncic, his inspired defensive play is aimed at proving his naysayers wrong.

Lakers star Luka Doncic prevents the ball from going out of bounds in front of Toronto forward Scottie Barnes during the first half Sunday at Crypto.com Arena. (Scott Strazzante / Associated Press)

"Look, people are going to talk bad no matter what," Doncic said. "So I just try to focus on me, on my team, on what I can give to the team better. Like I said before, I think I made a huge step forward on both ends. So I just got to keep going like that."

Doncic taking the charges impressed his coaches and teammates the most because it showed he was willing to give up his body to make a stop.

"Even last season, before last season, I don't think I had maybe five charges in seven years, or six years," Doncic said. "So, that gets everybody fired up. ... I mean, it's going to show in statistics, but not much. ... I just wanted to get better at that, and three charges is not bad for one game."

Read more: How the Lakers' Luka Doncic went from 'Wonder Boy' to 'The Man'

Redick said he was amazed by Doncic's offensive exploits. Then he praised Doncic for his "awesome" play on defense.

"I think just his on-ball throughout the early stretch of games has been really good just in terms of containment," Redick said. "He's doing a great job talking on defense. Beyond just the steals and the charges and the rebounding.

"Fifteen defensive rebounds, just phenomenal."

Doncic entered the game leading the NBA in scoring, averaging 36.2 points per game. In his last three games before Sunday, Doncic scored 52 against the Jazz, 41 versus the Trail Blazers and 37 against the Warriors.

So Sunday was just another "normal" game for Doncic.

"It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal," Redick said. "We live on a spaceship and we're going at the speed of light at all times when he's on the court. When he has it going, it's like, pick your poison, cause he can just make any shot. And then you start putting two on the ball and everybody else is the beneficiary of that. He's a terrific offensive engine."

Ziaire Williams missed his third consecutive game, but Redick said a scan on the forward's ailing left foot was "clean."

"I would describe it [as] soreness that just pops up in the morning and he's feeling a lot better," Redick said. "I think just being, again, cautious with the back to back."

The questions the Lakers had to face as they returned to Southern California after a one-game trip to the Bay Area revolved around how this new group would respond to early-season adversity.

The answer: Pretty well, for the most part.

Less than 48 hours after blowing a 25-point lead that resulted in a 17-point loss to the Warriors, the Lakers bounced back with a 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday night at Crypto.com Arena to improve to 5-2 on the season.

Luka Doncic continued his brilliant start to the season. NBAE via Getty Images

Luka Dončić once again got off to a hot start en route to a spectacular performance.

The Slovenian superstar finished with 45 points (12-for-23 shooting, 8 of 12 on 3-pointers), 15 rebounds, six assists and five steals in 35 minutes against the Raptors.

It was his second 40-point, 10-rebound, five-steal game as a Laker, and he's still the only player in franchise history to reach those statistical benchmarks in a game.

Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket against the Toronto Raptors on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images

Dončić, the league's leading scorer, has scored at least 37 points in four consecutive games.

The Lakers controlled most of the game, leading by as many as 26 points early in the third.

The Raptors cut their deficit down to nine midway through the fourth before the Lakers regained composure.

But once coach JJ Redick emptied the bench with his team having what seemed to be a comfortable 14-point lead, the Lakers quickly lost control of the game, with the Raptors going on a 11-2 run to cut their deficit to 125-120 before Redick subbed Doncic, Reaves, Kessler and Matisse Thybulle back in with 44 seconds left.

Kenneth Walker ran for 3 yards to the 1 before Patrick Surtain tackled him; Mahomes threw incomplete; and Walker was stopped for no gain by safety JL Skinner. That set up a final play with four seconds left, and after a false start, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes to end the game.

The Chiefs outgained the Broncos 399 to 294 as Mahomes went 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns. Johnson caught five passes for 128 yards and a touchdown and had a 15-yard run. Kelce added five catches for 67 yards.

Bo Nix was 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, going 5-of-6 for 84 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Coleman had 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown and four catches for 63 yards.

#2771. Preview: Utah Jazz hit the Road to Play Wemby’s Spurs

The season is by no means lost, but the Jazz need a win in the worst way right now. That said, the Jazz hit the road to Texas to face the reigning Western Conference Champion San Antonio Spurs and Victor Wembanyama… Everything but an easy win for a struggling Jazz squad.

While the early-season homestand was not kind to the Jazz in the win-loss column or on the injury report, they have shown flashes of improvement in several areas, game by game. Now it is simply a matter of putting it all together for a full 48-minute game. Pardon my galaxy-brain take here, but at the end of the day, basketball comes down to making shots and outscoring your opponent. The Jazz could improve offensively in several ways. You can talk about putting more pressure on the rim, forcing turnovers leading to easier baskets, second-chance points, etc. One of the biggest things that needs to change if the Jazz want to win more games, including against this formidable Spurs squad, is that shooters like Lauri Markkanen, Svi Mykhailiuk, Keyonte George, and Brice Sensabaugh need to shoot it and shoot it well against the Spurs.

Keyonte George has shot the ball very well with the exception of the Halloween game vs. Portland (we will blame the spooky vibes in the air for that performance), but Lauri Markkanen has been utterly putrid shooting the ball so far this year, shooting only 30% from three. Similarly, Svi Mykhailiuk, who was viewed as a key rotational piece coming into the season, is shooting 26% from three. Both of those guys need to make shots and produce in a meaningful way if the Jazz want to beat the Spurs, as Wemby does not allow much at the rim.

Defensively, there is no real way to stop Wemby; you can only hope he doesn't go absolutely nuclear on you. If the Jazz can win the rebounding battle as they did in Salt Lake on October 28th, they will give themselves a chance to pull off the upset.

Where: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio, Texas

How to Watch: KJZZ, Jazz+, NBA League Pass

#2769. Kaima Taira, Hiromi Itoh among Japanese pitchers posted to MLB

A pair of Japanese pitchers will be posted to Major League Baseball, their NPB clubs announced over the weekend.

The Seibu Lions announced on Saturday they plan to post Japanese pitcher Kaima Taira. On Sunday, the Nippon-Ham Fighters announced they will post ace right-hander Hiromi Itoh.

Players from NPB can be posted any time from November 1 to December 5, and once posted they have 45 days to sign. But expect any Japanese players to be posted on the early end this offseason, with a lockout coming on December 1 at 8:59 p.m. PT.

Players at least 25 years old with at least six years of professional experience in a foreign league can be signed as a major league free agent, rather than be subject to international amateur signing bonus limits like Roki Sasaki was before the 2025 season.

Taira turns 27 years old on November 15 and has pitched nine seasons for Seibu, mostly in relief but some starting. He had a 1.36 ERA with 141 strikeouts and 45 walks in 146 innings in his 23 games in 2026, after a 1.71 ERA and 31 games in 52 2/3 innings in 2025.

"As a pitcher, my goal is to win a Cy Young award," the Japanese news agency Kyodo quoted him as saying. "And I'd like to pitch in the World Series as well."

In his nine seasons with Seibu, the right-hander has a 1.85 ERA with 676 strikeouts and 252 walks in 633 2/3 innings over 351 games.

Itoh had a 3.18 ERA in 26 games last year for the Fighters, with 159 strikeouts and 34 walks in 172 2/3 innings. The 29-year-old right-hander in six years in NPB had a 2.91 ERA with 914 strikeouts and 247 walks in 1008 2/3 innings.

Michael Clair at MLB.com talked to a Pacific Rim scout about Itoh, Taira, and two other Japanese players expected to be posted to MLB this offseason. On Itoh:

"He could be an up and down starter," our scout said, "but maybe in relief he might show some more velocity. In the previous WBC, he came out of the bullpen and he was 94-96 with some nasty stuff." However, what Itoh lacks in size, he makes up for with a deep pitch mix consisting of "10+ unique grips and shapes" as noted by Yakyu Cosmopolitan.

Should he come to the Majors next year, there is one thing Itoh would like to share: "I would like the fans in the U.S. and everywhere else to know that I am not just pitching, but that I enjoy myself on the mound," Itoh told me this spring. "I like to express my excitement and joy."

Three Japanese players were posted last offseason. First baseman Munetaka Murakami signed with the Chicago White Sox for two years, $34 million. Third baseman Kazuma Okamoto signed for four years, $60 million with the Toronto Blue Jays. Pitcher Tatsua Imai signed with the Houston Astros for three years, $54 million.

#2768. Ravens may explore trading for Tyson Bagent

The Baltimore quarterback room was decimated on Sunday. With nine days left in the trading period, the Ravens could start looking for help elsewhere.

Starter Lamar Jackson is heading to injured reserve with a thumb injury that could end his season. Backup Tyler Huntley has a toe injury; its severity is to be determined.

One name to watch, as mentioned on Football Night in America, is Tyson Bagent. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle had that same position last year in Chicago. And the Bears have three quarterbacks.

Bagent has a $4 million salary in 2026, and a $4.25 million compensation package in 2027. The Bears also have Case Keenum under contract, behind Caleb Williams.

The Ravens, we’re told, may explore the possibility of acquiring Bagent. We’re also told that it won’t be cheap to get him.

That’s how it goes when a team develops an in-season need for a quarterback. The price goes up, as reflected by the urgency of the effort to find a replacement.

If Huntley will miss time, the Ravens need to do something. The only other quaterback on the roster is Joe Fagnone, who played after Jackson and Huntley were hurt.

The Ravens have no quarterbacks on the practice squad. Diego Pavia was on the 90-man roster in the offseason; he was cut just before the opening of training camp. Austin Reed was later signed to the roster during camp, after Skylar Thompson was placed on injured reserve.

#2766. Nets visit Knicks with fresh memories of terrible 2025-26 blowouts

INDIANAPOLIS — The Nets got their first win but won't have long to savor it. They'll face the champion Knicks Monday in the Garden, which has become their own house of horrors.

The Nets crossed the East River twice last season, losing the first 134-98 on Nov. 9 and then an even worse loss Jan. 21, 120-66.

That second one was the biggest loss in the history of the rivalry, the second biggest in Nets history, and still sticks in their craw. At least, Michael Porter Jr. says it should.

Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. has not forgotten how his team lost in historic fashion at the Garden last Jan. 21, when they were obliterated by 54 points. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post

"We've got a big game [Monday] that we should be very excited to play," Porter said. "Last year, when we went to the Garden, it was not pretty, and we should remember that and look forward to getting our rest [Sunday night] and going in there and being competitive. I know I'm looking forward to it."

Julius Randle, who made three All-Star games in his five years playing for the Knicks, will face his old team for the first time as a Net.

"I'm sure it'll be a lot of fun," said Randle, unaware of the recent blowouts.

"No, I don't know nothing about it. I live in the present, baby. … Focus on what we need to do to get a win, build off of what we did [Sunday] and stick together as a group."

Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. did not play Sunday but is set to return Monday against the Knicks. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Nets will get some reinforcements for Monday.

Mikel Brown Jr. missed the win in Indiana with back injury management. The Nets downplayed any concerns, and head coach Jordi Fernández confirmed the rookie is expected back against the Knicks.

Brown has been under a minutes limit and remains so. The point guard logged a career-high 28 minutes in Tuesday's loss in Boston, then 23 in a disappointing home loss to the Pistons on Friday.

Day'Ron Sharpe had 15 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and hit his only 3-point attempt Sunday. The points and boards were season highs and marked the fourth time in his career he'd had at least 13 points and 13 rebounds.

"Unbelievable. He was big on the boards. He did a little of everything: He made his 3. He set screens. Very happy for him. We don't win this game without him, and the reality is how much he cares about winning and impacting winning," Fernández said.

"I told him finally he gets more than 10 rebounds. I think he can do that night in, night out, get 10-plus rebounds. And if he does that, we're gonna be a hard team to beat, especially if he's getting four offensive rebounds," Porter said. "As long as he's a force, he's getting fouled on the glass — that's his superpower — if we're getting that from him, then we're really happy, for sure."

#2765. The Metropolitan Division in Review: 9/29—11/1

Good morning, Devils fans. Along with Jackson's article today, we are going to take a look at how each team in the Metropolitan Division is faring through the first month (roughly) of the season. Each team will have their major transactions and injuries summarized along with a piece of commentary.

Signing: Alexander Nikishin on a one-year contract — 10/25/26

Jordan Staal (C) — Torn Calf, 1-2 Months — 10/13/26

Taylor Hall (LW) — Upper-Body, Week-to-Week — 10/13/26

Return: Seth Jarvis (W) — Offseason shoulder surgery — 10/21/26

The Carolina Hurricanes are off on what is now just a usual start for them. Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake are not just playing like middle six players, but producing like top-liners, allowing the team to work around the difficulties of having important players in and out of their lineup. Sebastian Aho, with nine goals and 21 points, is on pace for a career season. But more dangerous than any of those developments has been the goaltending of Pyotr Kochetkov, who is 10-0 with a .929 save percentage and 1.49 goals against average. Right now, it looks like Carolina is beatable when they have Brandon Bussi in net, but not so much otherwise. If the Devils hope to catch Carolina in the standings, the Hurricanes are going to have to do something they rarely seem to do: regress.

Recalled from Utica on 10/12 and reassigned to Utica on 10/20

Trade: Acquired Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Alex Command, Nick Bjugstad, 2029 2nd round pick, 2027 seventh-round pick — 10/23/26

Trade: Acquired a 7th round pick in 2027 from the Washington Capitals in exchange for Remi Poirier — 11/1/26

Return: Connor Brown (W) — Lower-body — 10/20/26

Return: Johnny Kovacevic (D — Offseason knee surgery — 10/10/26

Anthony Mantha (W) — Undisclosed — Left 10/30 game

The New Jersey Devils have been the most active team in the Metropolitan Division so far this season. Perhaps this assuaged some of the concerns that some had for the team, though certain media members may still be denying how dangerous they are now that they have Hellebuyck in goal. But even before Hellebuyck joined the roster, the Devils had a top-three shots rate in the league, though their numbers here took a hit in their latter back-t0-back game in Colorado last week. The really big developments for the Devils this season have been the steps that Luke Hughes and Arseny Gritsyuk have taken for the team, while Dougie Hamilton has been strong in both ends to start the season to form a great top two pairings of Hughes-Pesce and Siegenthaler-Hamilton. With one of the best bottom six groups in the league keeping pressure up on opponents, the Devils were even able to survive slow starts from their highest-paid forwards. If Jack Hughes continues what he did in Vegas, and if Timo Meier (1 goal, 5 points) can start scoring to give Nico Hischier (7 goals, 2 assists) more consistent appearances on the scoresheet, the Devils' offense will generally be too much for opponents to overcome now that Connor Hellebuyck (.923 SV% in two games) holds down the fort.

Trade: Acquired Remi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round pick — 11/1/26

Matt Roy (RHD) — Lower-Body; six games — Returned 10/20/26

Pierre-Luc Dubois (C) — Illness; five games — Returned 10/24/26

Never count the Washington Capitals out of anything. For all of the hand-wringing about whether Alex Ovechkin is really himself in his final season, as he plays bottom six minutes with only four points in 13 games, the team is outscoring opponents 9-7 in his minutes, and Ovechkin has started slowly before. Meanwhile, the team around him is not having an issue scoring thanks to new additions in Alex Tuch (10 goals) and Jordan Kyrou (11 points) despite Dubois' illness keeping him out of five contests. Cole Hutson also has four goals and eight points, while the Protas brothers have yet to get going much on offense. If Spencer Carbery actually uses Remi Poirier, the Capitals have the potential to be even better, as Logan Thompson and Charlie Lindgren have a combined .895 save percentage and 2.94 goals against average through 13 games.

#2761. A pattern emerges in Raptors losses, as do bright spots in LA

Sometimes, a loss is a miserable situation that gets called a learning experience to save face. But watching this game against the Lakers, I was, at times, genuinely heartened by the product that I saw on the floor. The result? Less heartening, that is for sure, but there's a lot to learn from this November 1st 131-125 game.

For one: the Raptors seemed willing to shoot threes, and make up for any inaccuracy with their rebounding and interior presence. And while they weren't always making them, it was nice to see, and helped them get back into the game, especially with Luka Dončić on the bench.

With the Magic-man out, the Raptors looked not only in control, but confident, even without Jakob Poeltl on the floor. Poeltl's absence meant a start from Trayce Jackson-Davis, who, despite sharing the job with Collin Murray-Boyles, looked good on the floor there in some limited minutes. The Bench Mob 2.0 came in during garbage time that didn't feel quite like garbage time: the Lakers put their starters back in during a two possession game, giving the reserves some valuable experience, punctuated by a Jamison Battle three, and an Allen Graves steal.

Both Darko Rajaković and Scottie Barnes got technical fouls tonight, a reality that showcases a Raptors team willing to fight for its position. While less than ideal in a big matchup, getting some of this energy out early helps to set the tone for the season. Speaking of that-

Scottie Barnes still looks fantastic, and had a great offensive game, posting stats of 29-6-5 along with two steals. He got 13 free throw attempts, drawing a lot of contact and getting the foul calls that his driving would warrant, even though he only made seven of those shots: less than ideal. Still, the player he is developing into is absolutely fantastic, capable of carrying the responsibility of a number-one offensive option, even though he's perhaps better suited to the place of a secondary or tertiary scorer.

RJ Barrett looked great, as usual, with a hyper-efficient 22 point night, that was marred only by the complete lack of free throws attempted. Adding on three steals to his statline, RJ looked impactful, and his big three to get the deficit back to single digits was a highlight of the night for the Raps.

LOS ANGELES, CA – NOVEMBER 1: Immanuel Quickley #5 of the Toronto Raptors drives to the basket during the game against the Los Angeles Lakers on November 1, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

However, efficiency was a major, major issue for the Raptors tonight. They shot 43% from the floor and 31% from three, which, while an attempted increase in volume explains, does not necessarily translate to much meaningful production for the Raptors. The Raptors' offence without Kawhi is supported in part around Scottie and RJ creating interior pressure, which should ideally create space for shooters like Immanuel Quickley or Ja'Kobe Walter, but tonight, the shots just weren't falling, especially from IQ, who went 3/11 from outside.

The Lakers, on the other hand, were shooting 60% from three at the half, which begs the question: were the Raptors unlucky two nights in a row, or does there need to be more effort at defence on the perimeter?

Very similarly to both of the Raptors' previous losses, the major issue came at the hands of volume scoring guards as opposed to big men, despite the oft-discussed issues that the Raptors have had at centre. Luka Dončić had 45 points tonight, and sometimes, when a scorer like Luka gets hot, there is no defence anywhere on heaven or Earth than can stop him from getting the ball to the cup. He shot 66% from three and went 100% from the charity stripe. This is very similar to what happened with Desmond Bane in the second Orlando game.

While the three remains a potent weapon against anyone, it seems that the Raptors are particularly susceptible to it. Sure, you shoot a dinosaur with a rifle and it falls over, but Toronto needs to teach its predators how to strap on bulletproof vests. The Raptors are a great defensive team, but this is a weakness that has now cropped up twice as a pattern, and needs to be eliminated before it becomes the Raptors' Achilles heel. This is, of course, the Raptors playing without Kawhi Leonard, which means that they've lost arguably their best offensive player, and some very important perimeter D.

Tonight was also a game without Jakob Poeltl, meaning that the Raps were playing without two of their most important pieces. Poeltl was out with shoulder bursitis, which the Cleveland Clinic notes varies in severity and frequency. His injury circumstances are not yet clear. This situation is even more distressing when considering the fact that both Poeltl and Leonard are notorious for missing time. If this is how the Raptors will perform regularly under such circumstances, there is indeed some serious concern here for the functioning of the team.

Should the LA game be moment of total panic and abandon for the Raptors and their fans? No. Luka Dončić is one of the best scorers in the world, and without two starters, the Raptors were always going to be fighting an uphill battle to keep up tonight.

The Raptors have not even played ten games yet and should not be written off as mere pretenders, but, this series may give the indication that the Raptors playing their reserves as starters may put them firmly in the place they were last year: solid enough to beat the bad teams, and not great enough to beat the good ones.

Leonard is set to be evaluated and the degree to which his injury will keep him off the floor will become clearer in the upcoming week. His health for the season and production upon returning will be the yardstick by which this season's success will be measured. Until then, the Raptors have another LA matchup to look forward to, this time, against a team they are well acquainted with. The… Los Angeles Clippers.

#2760. Frustrated Justin Jefferson didn't speak to reporters after Sunday's loss

When a team is winning, it’s hard for any offensive players who aren’t getting the ball as often as they should to be upset. When winning becomes losing, the frustrations can quickly surface.

That happened for the Vikings on Sunday against the Lions. Receiver Justin Jefferson, who made a spectacular touchdown catch in the first half, didn’t see the ball as often as he should have during proverbial nut-cutting time.

After the Vikings’ final drive — which curiously ended on a fourth-and-five punt with 3:01 to play at a time when the Detroit rushing game was clicking — Jefferson made a rare display of frustration. After the 19-15 loss, Jefferson declined to speak to reporters, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.

Which means that Jefferson, who has a habit of always saying all the right things, doubted that he would have been able to do that.

“Obviously he’s frustrated, and that’s understandable,” quarterback Kyler Murray told reporters, via Seifert. “He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn’t get the ball. That’s on us to find a way to get him the ball.”

“We had some opportunities for [Jefferson], and there were some chances there,” coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters. “But we’ve got to find a way to get him the ball, especially on potential chances for him on some of those sequences where we’re looking to kick off some momentum. He’s a great guy to do it behind, and we’ll continue to find ways to get him the football. But it was a division game. These guys want to win. I don’t fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form.”

Whatever the cause, there’s clearly a problem. And Murray, who missed time early in the season due to a concussion, should be up to speed now. On Sunday, he wasn’t good enough.

And here’s the basic reality. At some point, either en route to the playoffs or after the Vikings get there, Murray will have to make a big play in a big spot. The jury is out on whether he will.

The Vikings don’t have many options. They could try to make a trade, but who’s out there? They wanted to keep Daniel Jones after the 2024 season; maybe, at this point, the Colts would welcome the chance to move on.

If the Raiders had lost to the Jets, Kirk Cousins may have been available for a reunion. With Las Vegas now at 4-4, why would they move him?

The other option would be to ride with Carson Wentz, who has shown that he can and will get the ball to Jefferson.

However it goes, Sunday’s game exposed the biggest problem with the Vikings. Against teams that can’t be held to 15 points or less, the Vikings may not be able to muster enough points to beat them.

#2758. Dak Prescott: "Cowardice" to put blame for Sunday's loss on Brian Schottenheimer

The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead and lost at home for the first time in franchise history on Sunday, so quarterback Dak Prescott may have been understating things when he called it “one of the toughest” losses of his career.

Arizona scored 20 points in the final 11 minutes of regulation and then missed an extra point that would have given them a win. That reprieve did not spark the Cowboys as they went three-and-out on their only possession before the Cardinals’ game-winning field goal in overtime.

The magnitude of the collapse during a season that has featured other underwhelming performances has led to questions about head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s job security. Prescott was adamant after the loss that all can’t be put on Schottenheimer’s shoulders.

“It’s all of us,” Prescott said, via the team’s website. “Don’t put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardice. This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It’s never just one person’s fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it’s never just truly one person’s fault. And so, don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it’s about us backing him up and backing one another up and we’ll have to show it.”

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he’s not thinking about an in-season coaching change, but he also called the loss an “indictment of the whole show” and Schottenheimer’s job puts him at the top of the pyramid. That could wind up working out well for him if the 3-5 team can navigate its way past the Giants to win the NFC East, but there’s been little about their performance to this point in the season to suggest they’re capable of that kind of consistent success.

#2757. Luka Dončić has taken a step forward defensively for the Lakers this season

LOS ANGELES — Luka Dončić has heard it all.

He can't play defense. He's a showman, a front runner, a whiny shot-chucker whose game isn't conducive to winning. He can average all the stats he wants. It won't translate to anything.

Sunday night, in the Lakers' 131-125 win over the Toronto Raptors, he proved that he's more than what people say he is.

He's just a great basketball player. Perhaps the best in the world.

Every time Dončić went to the free throw line on Sunday, he was met with "M-V-P" chants from the Crypto.com Arena crowd.

It wasn't just the 45 points and eight 3-pointers that inspired the ovation. It was also the defensive engagement, the 15 rebounds (all defensive), five steals and three drawn charges over 35 minutes, each second more crucial than the next. It was the product of an initiative he set for himself ahead of this season.

"Obviously I'm not the best defender in the NBA," Dončić said postgame. "But I think this year I really took a step forward. Obviously people are going to talk what they want to talk. The media is going to talk what they want to talk, but my team knows that [and] I think that I'm better this year, and that helps the whole team."

The ninth-year superstar entered Sunday's game averaging a league-leading 36.2 points per game, a figure that's only going up after another offensive onslaught. And yet, as he averages 43.8 points over his last four contests, it's as much his defensive activity that's inspiring the Lakers.

"He's been awesome on defense," head coach JJ Redick said Sunday. "Even his on-ball [pressure] throughout this early stretch of games has been really good in terms of containment. … He's doing a great job just talking on defense beyond just the steals and the charges and the rebounding. Fifteen defensive rebounds. Just phenomenal."

Players of Dončić's offensive caliber, who are relied on as much as he is, are often less willing to sacrifice their bodies on the other end of the floor. But for Dončić, as quiet and mild-tempered as he is off the floor, standing in front of a driving opponent and risking his body in the moment signals something greater.

"I think taking a charge in general is just a form of leadership," Redick said. "Putting your body on the line for the team. He's just trying to win. You see the competitiveness come out so many times on the offensive end, but he's competitive on the defensive end, too."

When Walker Kessler listed off the players on the roster that would contribute to Los Angeles having one of the best defenses in the league, even he overlooked Dončić.

Kessler thought he was brought in to complement the star's offensive game as a roller and make the game easier for him by anchoring the defense. He never thought he'd have to match Dončić's level of defensive contribution.

"Incredible," Kessler said. "Luka doesn't get enough credit for his defense. He's a very high IQ individual when it comes to being on the court. His positional defense is being in the right spot at the right time, and it is really good and it showed tonight.

"[When] all the players see a guy like him, who's a savant on the offensive side, be so good defensively, it gets to the guys. It hypes them up to play better defense. So, yeah, it was incredible."

Dončić put up averages no one in NBA history has replicated in the two seasons he was high in the MVP race ('23-24 and '25-26), but he was never truly in the conversation. He's dealt with this his entire career.

Defense has been the main excuse used to rule him out of the award race. This year, the Lakers are a plus-87 with Dončić on the floor. And guess what? He's playing on both ends of the floor now.

It's still very early, but this is what an MVP looks like.

#2756. Baker Mayfield on zero completed passes: Whatever it takes to win

The Buccaneers set a franchise-record with 324 rushing yards in Sunday’s 16-0 win over the Falcons and they made a little other history as well.

The Bucs did not have a completed pass in the game, which was a first in franchise history and it made them the first team since the Bills in 1974 to go an entire game without completing a pass. The game was played in wet and sloppy conditions that joined Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield’s injured right thumb as reasons why the Bucs only tried three passes all game.

“I’ll do whatever it takes to win,” Mayfield said, via Rob Maaddi of the Associated Press. “That’s all that matters to me.”

Mayfield was 7-of-11 in Tampa’s Week 7 win over the Panthers and the team has called a total of 16 pass plays over the last two weeks. They’ve called 104 running plays and the back-to-back wins should serve as proof of concept for a run-focused approach no matter the weather in the weeks to come.
